name: text-reveal-card

frames.best_why: Frame 4 uncovers the most of the bright line, with the divider bar mid-card and the dim text still behind.

tagline: Sweep the cursor across the card to wipe one sentence over another.
summary: A dark card shows a faint sentence that a second, brighter message replaces wherever your pointer has crossed. A thin divider bar rides the cursor edge, and the reveal snaps back when you leave.
appearance: A wide dark grey card with a thin border holds a small white heading and a grey hint line at the top. Across its lower half a large bold sentence sits dim grey among drifting white specks; up to the pointer the same line appears bright white behind a narrow vertical bar.
behaviour: Sliding the pointer across the card uncovers a bright copy of the sentence from the left, tracking the cursor with no lag, while a thin divider bar tilts and follows. Leaving the card retracts the reveal to nothing and fades the bar out.
demo_content: Heading "Sometimes, you just need to see it." above the lines "You know the business" and "I know the chemistry".
search_phrases: card that wipes away to show a message
before and after sentence comparison card
scrub across to reveal another line
use_when: You want a small surprising reward for moving the cursor over a card of copy.
avoid_when: Touch or keyboard readers need the hidden line, or the card must fit a narrow column.
customise: text and revealText set the two sentences, and children fill the header. The fixed forty-rem width, colours and the star field need a source edit.
weight_why: Eighty drifting star dots plus a pointer-tracked clip-path reveal.

a11y.note: The hidden line can only be uncovered by pointer or touch, with no keyboard route, and the star drift ignores reduced-motion.

issues: The resting sentence is dark grey on dark grey, so it is almost unreadable before the reveal.
Only a pointer or touch uncovers the hidden line; keyboard users cannot reach it.
polish_why: Smooth cursor reveal and tidy divider, but the resting line is nearly invisible and the header tiny.
